questions.question: The initial value of position is?
questions.explanation: The initial value of the position property is static.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: The initial value of the position property is static.

questions.question: When is an element 'positioned'?
options: When position is anything other than static.
questions.explanation: When you change this value to anything else, the element is said to be positioned. An element with static positioning is thus not positioned.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: When you change this value to anything else, the element is said to be positioned.

questions.question: How is positioning different from flex and grid?
options: It is the same as flex-direction.
It can remove elements from document flow entirely.
questions.explanation: Positioning is different: it removes elements from the document flow entirely. This allows you to place the element somewhere else on the screen.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: it removes elements from the document flow entirely.

questions.question: Grant lists which types in the chapter opener?
options: Fixed, relative, and absolute, plus sticky as a new type.
questions.explanation: The types of element positioning: fixed, relative, and absolute. A new type: sticky.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: The types of element positioning: fixed, relative, and absolute

questions.question: Duckett's layout chapter will explore?
options: Normal flow, relative positioning, absolute positioning and floats.
questions.explanation: Explore different ways to position elements using normal flow, relative positioning, absolute positioning and floats.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Explore different ways to position elements using normal flow, relative positioning, absolute positioning and floats.

questions.question: position: relative then top/left does what?
options: Offsets the box from where it would have been; the original space remains.
Pins the box to the viewport.
questions.explanation: Relative offset is from the element's static position. Inclusive Components uses relative plus top/left on a toggle.

questions.question: What can overlapping positioned elements do?
options: Sit in front of or behind one another.
Only sit in document order, never paint order.
questions.explanation: It can place elements in front of or behind one another, thus overlapping one another.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: It can place elements in front of or behind one another, thus overlapping one another.

questions.question: absolute is placed relative to?
options: The nearest positioned ancestor, or the page if none.
questions.explanation: Absolute takes the element out of flow. The containing block is the nearest positioned ancestor.

questions.question: Why do dropdowns and modals show up in this chapter?
options: The position property is what you use to build dropdown menus, modal dialogs, and similar.
They cannot be built with CSS.
questions.explanation: the position property, which you can use to build dropdown menus, modal dialogs, and other essential effects.

options: A newer type of positioning listed in the chapter.

questions.question: z-index fights are often really?
options: Stacking context problems — a positioned ancestor with z-index creates a new context.
questions.explanation: Understanding the stacking context will keep you out of trouble when the wrong elements sit in front of others.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: Understanding the stacking context will keep you out of trouble

questions.question: Should you lay out a two-column page with absolute on every box?
options: Yes; that is Grant's recommended page layout.
No. Flow methods (flex, grid, even floats) keep document flow. Absolute is for overlays.
Yes, if you also set z-index: 9999.
Absolute is required for columns in HTML5.
questions.explanation: Previous chapters manipulated document flow. Positioning removes elements from it. Columns want flow.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: The layout methods we’ve covered in previous chapters do various things to manipulate the way document flow behaves.

questions.question: Which pair makes a containing block for an absolute child?
questions.explanation: A positioned ancestor (relative here) is the containing block. static does not count as positioned.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: An element with static positioning is thus not positioned.

questions.question: top / right / bottom / left do nothing useful while position is static because?
options: The element is not positioned, so offsets are not applied that way.
questions.explanation: Offsets apply to positioned boxes. static is the initial, not-positioned value.
